about: Generated by scripts/sync-plugin.mjs from the awards repository. Do not edit by hand.

rules.message: Reflex typeface used as the first family
rules.fix: Pick a face by character class (references/reflex-lists.md); if this face is a deliberate choice, record it under AWARDS.md ## Exceptions

rules.message: Google Fonts CDN link
rules.fix: Self-host the woff2 files with font-display and a size-adjusted fallback

rules.message: Display size above 12vw or unclamped vw
rules.fix: Lock display type to the artboard with clamp(min, Xvw, max), max ≈ 12–13vw

rules.message: Letter-spacing tighter than -0.06em
rules.fix: Set display tracking at -0.04em or looser by choice; past -0.06em the letters collide at display sizes

rules.message: @font-face without font-display
rules.fix: Add font-display: swap (or optional for decorative faces) to avoid invisible text

rules.message: No size-adjust fallback face
rules.fix: Declare a metric-compatible fallback with size-adjust/ascent-override to avoid reflow when the real face lands

rules.message: Body text set against reading (justified, capitals, tight leading, wide tracking or under 14px)
rules.fix: Running text wants ragged-right, sentence case, leading 1.4–1.6, normal tracking and at least 16px; keep the effects for display lines

rules.message: Flat type hierarchy (h1 under 1.5× the body size, rendered)
rules.fix: Let the scale carry the hierarchy: a display step well clear of body, then fewer, wider steps

rules.message: Text contrast below 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text)
rules.fix: Adjust ink or ground; large text (24 px, or 18.66 px bold) may use 3:1, all other text needs 4.5:1, measured against what is actually behind it and in the focus state

rules.message: Pure #000 or #fff ground
rules.fix: Use a warm or cool near-black/off-white unless pure black is diegetic; record diegetic use under AWARDS.md ## Exceptions

rules.message: More than 6 distinct hues in the tokens
rules.fix: Winners run 2–4 tokens; variety comes from change over time, not simultaneity

rules.message: Gradient text
rules.fix: Emphasis comes from weight, size or a colour field, not background-clip: text

rules.message: Ground differs from the DESIGN.md ground token (rendered)
rules.fix: Paint body (and main, when it has a fill) with the ground token, or correct DESIGN.md to the ground the world actually uses

rules.message: No prefers-reduced-motion branch anywhere
rules.fix: Add a reduced tier (no spatial movement; keep opacity/colour/state) via CSS media query and gsap.matchMedia / matchMedia in JS

rules.message: Global 0.01ms animation kill under reduced motion
rules.fix: Reduced motion is a tier, not a kill switch: keep feedback and state transitions

rules.message: Scrubbed tween with an ease other than none
rules.fix: Scroll-linked tweens must use ease: 'none'; the scrub value supplies the smoothing

rules.message: will-change applied broadly
rules.fix: Apply will-change only during a known animation and only to the moving element

rules.message: CSS scroll-behavior: smooth together with a smooth-scroll library
rules.fix: Remove scroll-behavior: smooth; Lenis owns scrolling

rules.message: pin: true used alongside position: sticky
rules.fix: Prefer sticky stages with invisible rails; if pinning, do not also make the element sticky

rules.message: Animating a layout property (width/height/top/left/margin)
rules.fix: Animate transforms, clip-path or use FLIP; layout properties force reflow every frame

rules.message: Infinite loop without a visibility/intersection pause
rules.fix: Pause repeat:-1 loops when the tab is hidden or the element is off-screen

rules.message: Missing <main> landmark
rules.fix: Wrap the page content in <main>; add <header>/<nav>/<footer> where they exist

rules.message: without alt
rules.fix: Write alt text (or alt="" for decorative images)

rules.message: Heading structure broken (no h1, several h1, or skipped levels)
rules.fix: One h1 per page; no skipped levels; visual size comes from CSS, not from the heading level

rules.message: <canvas> without aria-hidden or an accessible name
rules.fix: Mark decorative canvases aria-hidden="true" and keep a semantic DOM mirror of any text drawn in WebGL

rules.message: Click handler on a div/span
rules.fix: Use <button> or <a>; they come with keyboard and focus behaviour for free

rules.message: No :focus-visible style
rules.fix: Theme the focus ring from the tokens; it is a browser surface that carries the design

rules.message: outline: none without a replacement focus style
rules.fix: Keep :focus-visible styling when removing default outlines

rules.message: Custom cursor without a coarse-pointer guard
rules.fix: Enable custom cursors only under (pointer: fine) and (hover: hover); hide them on touch

rules.message: <html> without lang
rules.fix: Set lang on <html>

rules.message: Autoplay video without muted/playsinline
rules.fix: Autoplay requires muted and playsinline; add a poster and respect reduced motion

rules.message: Pointer-only interaction (drag/hold) without a keyboard handler
rules.fix: Every gesture needs a keyboard equivalent (arrow keys, Enter/Space, Escape)

rules.message: Focus ring below 3:1 against what surrounds it (rendered)
rules.fix: Take the ring colour from the tokens and check it at 3:1 against every ground it can sit on (WCAG 2.2 non-text contrast); offset it or add a second contrasting ring where one colour cannot reach both

rules.message: Navigation without a skip link
rules.fix: Make the first focusable element a same-page link that skips to <main> (visible on focus)

rules.message: Touch target under 24 px beside another target (rendered, phone)
rules.fix: Give each control at least 24 × 24 px, or 24 px of clear space from its neighbours (WCAG 2.2 target size); aim for 44 px on the primary actions

rules.message: Duplicate id
rules.fix: Make every id unique; labels, aria references and fragment links resolve to the first one only

rules.message: axe-core reports a WCAG 2.2 A/AA violation (rendered)
rules.fix: Fix what axe names at the node it points to; serious and critical impacts block, moderate and minor are P2

rules.message: Viewport meta stops pinch zoom (user-scalable=no or maximum-scale under 2)
rules.fix: Drop user-scalable and maximum-scale from the viewport meta; a gesture the page needs is handled with touch-action on that element, never by locking zoom (WCAG 1.4.4)

rules.message: Touch target under 44 × 44 px on a phone (rendered); the jury's usability walk caps Usability at 7 on it
rules.fix: Give the control a 44 × 44 px hit area under (pointer: coarse) with padding or min-height, keeping the type as drawn; links inside running text are exempt

rules.message: Fixed width above 600px
rules.fix: Use fluid widths, max-width or vw-locked values

rules.message: 100vw width can overflow with a vertical scrollbar
rules.fix: Use 100% or inline-size with overflow-x: clip on the container

rules.message: Missing viewport meta
rules.fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

rules.message: Identical card grid (icon + heading + text × n)
rules.fix: Cards are the lazy container; vary structure by content or use a list, a rail or poster blocks

rules.message: Eyebrow/kicker label above a heading, BEM parts like hero__eyebrow included
rules.fix: Delete the label; let the heading carry its own weight. Keep it only when WORLD names a metadata world (catalogue, archive, spec sheet, call sheet, timetable), with audit-ignore: L05

rules.message: Content stuck invisible after load (rendered)
rules.fix: Reveals start from a visible state or are set by the same code that animates them; a failed script or a skipped trigger must leave text readable

rules.message: Line length above 90 characters (rendered)
rules.fix: Cap running text at about 60–75ch with max-width on the text column, not the section

rules.message: Body text touching the viewport edge on a phone (rendered)
rules.fix: Give the text column the gutter token on both sides at every width

rules.message: Blank band: a whole viewport with no content in it (rendered)
rules.fix: Fill it, shorten the spacer or the pin, or check that the section meant to sit there renders at this width; a deliberate pause goes under AWARDS.md ## Exceptions

rules.message: Lopsided section on tablet or phone: content keeps to one narrow side (rendered)
rules.fix: Let the column take the width at this breakpoint, or balance the empty side with the section's own media; deliberate asymmetry goes under ## Exceptions

rules.message: Text, a heading or an action covered by something painted over it at every scroll position where it is in view (rendered)
rules.fix: Move the covering layer (a picture, a filled panel, a drawn line, a cast shadow) off the text's box, or give the text a lane of its own; a layer that passes over text it leaves readable at another position (a curtain, clouds, a stacked panel) is not counted, nor is a small fixed header, a canvas (its pixels are judged from the frames) or a duplicate of the same text

rules.message: Outer margins differ left and right at desktop width (rendered)
rules.fix: Set one pair of page margins and hang the navigation and every text block from them; keep asymmetry inside the grid, never in the frame

rules.message: Lopsided section on desktop: text in one half and nothing in the other (rendered)
rules.fix: Close the empty side with the section's own picture, a second column, a list or a figure, or let the text take the width; a void is placed only when something closes it

rules.message: A section of running text with no heading naming it (rendered)
rules.fix: Open the section with a heading in the heading face that names what it holds (“The rooms”, “Prices”), set on the page's anchor line; a small label is not a heading

rules.message: Two or more screens that are mostly plain ground (rendered)
rules.fix: Make the main element larger, bring the section's picture or full content into the screen, or take the space out; one deliberate rest per page, closed by something on its far side

rules.message: without width/height or loading attribute
rules.fix: Set width/height (or aspect-ratio) to avoid layout shift; lazy-load images below the fold

rules.message: Raster image above 1 MB
rules.fix: Export WebP/AVIF at the display size; keep the largest image under ~300 KB

rules.message: glTF/GLB without Draco or Meshopt compression in the loader
rules.fix: Compress with gltf-transform (draco/meshopt) and textures to KTX2; wire DRACOLoader/KTX2Loader

rules.message: Entry JS above 300 KB gzipped
rules.fix: Split WebGL and heavy libraries into lazy chunks; target ≈ 200 KB gz for the entry

rules.message: Too many or too heavy font files
rules.fix: Subset to the used ranges, ship ≤ 4 woff2 files, ≤ 400 KB total, preload the display face

rules.message: Uncapped devicePixelRatio for a WebGL renderer
rules.fix: renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2)) and cap the absolute pixel count on mobile

rules.message: WebGL renderer created without any dispose()
rules.fix: Dispose geometries, materials, textures and the renderer on route change

rules.message: Layout shift above 0.1 during load (rendered)
rules.fix: Reserve space for media, fonts and late content (width/height or aspect-ratio, size-adjust fallbacks, fixed slots); animate transform, never top, height or margin

rules.message: Image delivered below 1.5x the width it is drawn at (rendered)
rules.fix: Serve srcset candidates at 1.5x and 2x the drawn width (sizes from the layout), compressed to budget; a soft hero reads as unfinished on every phone

rules.message: No ::selection style
rules.fix: Theme selection from the tokens

rules.message: No scrollbar styling
rules.fix: scrollbar-color / ::-webkit-scrollbar in the palette (optional)

rules.message: No theme-color meta
rules.fix: Add <meta name="theme-color"> from the ground token

rules.message: No color-scheme declared
rules.fix: Add <meta name="color-scheme"> or html { color-scheme: … }

rules.message: No favicon
rules.fix: Ship an SVG favicon in the world's ink

rules.message: No Open Graph image
rules.fix: Author an OG image in the same world (1200×630)

rules.message: Page without a title
rules.fix: Give every page a <title> that names the page and the subject; it is the first thing a crawler, a tab and a share sheet read

rules.message: No meta description
rules.fix: Write one sentence per page in the voice of the site; it is the snippet a search result shows

rules.message: No Open Graph title or description
rules.fix: Add og:title and og:description beside og:image so a shared link carries the page, not the domain

rules.message: No canonical link
rules.fix: Add <link rel="canonical"> with the deployed URL of each page

rules.message: First screen without a readable h1 1.2 s after load (rendered)
rules.fix: A note for the jury, not a defect by itself: most measured winners open on a loader, an entrance or a film first (references/sites/_prevalence.md). Earn the wait or put the title in the HTML and paint it on the first frame; a canvas that draws it keeps a DOM mirror; a consent banner is not counted

rules.message: Generic CTA copy (Get started / Learn more)
rules.fix: Name the action in the product's own words, matched to the stakes

rules.message: Placeholder copy or images (lorem ipsum, placeholder hosts, empty src)
rules.fix: Author real content at full fidelity; label synthetic material

rules.message: Emoji used as icons
rules.fix: Use a drawn icon set with one stroke weight, or no icon

rules.message: backdrop-filter on many selectors (glass by default)
rules.fix: Glass is a specific effect, not a surface style; keep it to one earned moment

rules.message: Hard offset shadow (neo-brutalist costume)
rules.fix: Depth comes from luminance or optics unless the world is actually neo-brutalist

rules.message: Thick coloured side border on a card or callout
rules.fix: Remove the stripe; group by proximity and hierarchy instead

rules.message: Numbered section markers (01 / 02 / 03) or micro-meta (/ 01, No. 01)
rules.fix: Keep numbers only when the sequence carries meaning for the reader; P2 inside recipes/, which get copied

rules.message: Hero-metric template (big numbers row)
rules.fix: Numbers persuade as copy inside sentences (dual units, specifics), not as a stat row

rules.message: Decorative grid lines or stripes painted with gradients
rules.fix: A grid earns its lines when content sits on it; otherwise let the ground be a surface

rules.message: Coloured radial halo behind content
rules.fix: Light comes from the world (a photograph, a scene, a material), not a glow placed behind the headline

rules.message: Coloured glow shadow
rules.fix: Use depth by luminance or one material policy; neon glow is the default register, not a choice

rules.message: Generated palette (framework purple, violet or cyan; purple-to-pink gradient)
rules.fix: Derive ground and accent from the subject (references/reflex-lists.md); two to four tokens

rules.message: Bounce, elastic or overshoot easing
rules.fix: UI settles on the expo-out vocabulary; keep overshoot for a thing that is a character, and record it as an exception

rules.message: Decorative idle loop (pulse, ping, blink, float)
rules.fix: Motion answers an event or the scroll; an endless pulse says nothing changed. Keep it only where state is live

rules.message: Every image zooms or turns on hover
rules.fix: Pick one hover behaviour that carries information (a preview, a caption, a state) or leave images still

rules.message: Slogan antithesis repeated (“Not X. A Y.”)
rules.fix: State what the thing does, with a number or a verb; one turn of phrase per page at most

rules.message: Generic marketing claims
rules.fix: Replace each claim with the fact behind it: a number, a unit, a named feature, an outcome

rules.message: Em-dash habit
rules.fix: Most dashes want a full stop, a comma or a colon; keep the dash for a real interruption

rules.message: Hairline border plus wide soft shadow on one box
rules.fix: One edge per surface: a rule, a tone change or a shadow, not all at once

rules.message: Cards nested inside cards (rendered)
rules.fix: Flatten the inner level into rows or type; one container per idea

rules.message: Eyebrow labels above headings beyond one per three sections, by computed style (rendered)
rules.fix: Delete the labels the headings do not need; keep a set only when WORLD is a catalogue, index or spec sheet, and record it under ## Exceptions

patterns.title: Accessibility and reduced motion
patterns.lead: the part of the plugin that is deliberately better than its references. `[site:igloo]` scored 6.60 on Accessibility and 6.40 on Markup / Meta-data behind a 27-node DOM [verified, twenty Awwwards entries read 2026-09-18]; usability is the lowest axis on 27 of the 31 corpus entries awarded since 2021, and Accessibility is the lowest-ceilinged developer criterion of the six, at most 7.60 and at median 6.80 across the 30 corpus cards that publish it [verified per card; counted by `scripts/calibration.mjs --since 2021`, 2026-10-22] — a corpus figure, not a ceiling: Cartier's Site of the Day of 20 Oct 2026 scored 8.00 [verified, awwwards.com/sites/cartier-le-choeur-des-pierres read 2026-10-22]; and one card documents a reduced-motion path — Boc stops its rows, skips its case-open timeline and never mounts hover video, though it also ships a global `.01ms` duration clamp [site:boc] [verified]; Floema, the Anime.js source and Wodniack verifiably have none [clone:floema-jewelry] [site:animejs] [site:wodniack], Léo Parpeix appears to have none [site:leo-parpeix], the rest are unknown. The 2026-09-23 wave raises the floor [verified on each card]: reduced tiers that pass — each scroll effect jumped to its final state [site:mensch], every duration to .01 s with videos parked on posters [site:christoph-nagel], modules gated in code with 30 CSS blocks [site:okaydev], 57 branches [site:zainabkabira], WebGPU never created and grain frozen [site:warmnfuzzy] — against fifteen cards with no branch at all [site:robbietilton] [site:jesperlandberg] [site:wearedirect] [site:likova] [site:911rennsport] [site:siteassist] [site:to-top] [site:noth] [site:gehry-getty] [site:grids-obys] [site:serotoninn] [site:bethebuzz] [site:alectear] [site:siena] [site:the-boyd] and one that declares the query and never reads it [site:spasoje]. The 2026-10-05 wave [verified on each card]: no branch anywhere in a 100 % canvas descent [site:edolus]; a branch on route transitions and testimonials only, while the preloader, reveals, hero scrub and card fan ignore it [site:abatable]; passes — Lenis at `lerp 1` with instant scrolls and a gate that skips its throw [site:ascension-pegassi], static SVG strokes in place of the GL pipes [site:cyphercapital], reveals forced visible though Lenis still runs [site:eugeniagrab], a gallery that snaps instead of springing while its scribble still draws [site:a24-raviklaassens], a frame complete at rest over a sim that keeps running [site:aqualoqa]; partial — sequence stills but an unbranched load curtain and a still pointing at a missing file [site:aardvarkbookclub], a first reduced frame left empty [site:agrumeafarm], DOM transitions only and a film with no branch [site:cutobot-byholm]; fails — headings frozen as black goo [site:bleibtgleich] and a preloader mid-run with 8 of 18 builder interactions unbranched [site:stanzza]. The 2026-10-26 wave [verified on each card]: no `prefers-reduced-motion` anywhere, the reduced pass diving through full motion blur [site:everswap]; only a counter's digit slide stopped while the morph, starfield, flashes and trail run on [site:da-san333]; partial — the marquee, idle spin, fluid type, wake and hover shatter stop, but the object still travels between sections and the second world still plays, and the reduced frames show the same gate [site:daikifujita]. Everything below is therefore plugin policy, checked by the audit rules in brackets, and it is where new work beats the corpus instead of copying it. Cite as `[pattern:accessibility-and-reduced-motion#section]`.
sections: Skip link, landmarks and focus styles

patterns.title: Asset pipeline
patterns.lead: how the corpus turns gigabytes of DCC output into single-digit megabytes on the wire — the formats, the encoders, the budgets and the loading order — so that a cinematic scene ships at the weight of a hero image. Numbers come from the cards that published or exposed them; where a card is silent on formats (Oryzo, Slosh Seltzer, Trevor Noah, Seasats, Son Daven) this file says so instead of guessing. patterns.title: Colour and material
patterns.lead: how the corpus decides colour — how few tokens, which near-black, which ground, where the accent comes from, when colour is page state — and which material policy each world commits to. Read it while writing `DESIGN.md ## Colors` and `## Elevation & Depth` and generating `tokens.css`; cite it as `[pattern:color-and-material#section]`. Every hex here is a card's hex with its label; none is a value to reuse.

patterns.title: Components catalog
patterns.lead: the components the corpus builds more than once — what job each does, which cards ship it, what it is made of, how it moves, what it owes the keyboard and the reduced tier, which recipe builds it and which literal version is refused. Read it when filling the Components column of `AWARDS.md ## Page map` and when `DESIGN.md ## Components` is written; cite it as `[pattern:components-catalog#component]`. Every entry is a pattern, never a part to lift.

patterns.title: Consent and banners
patterns.lead: the consent banner, the one piece of chrome many winners let cover their own first viewport. It gives what the corpus records, the legal floor no further than the official sources go, the plugin's rules for placement, size, blocking, keyboard, motion and loading, and how a capture shows both the first visit and the clean page. Read it when the stack adds analytics, embeds or any third-party tag, and before `ship`. Cite it as `[pattern:consent-and-banners#section]`. This file is not legal advice. National laws transposing the ePrivacy Directive differ, and the client's counsel decides what the site needs.

patterns.title: Copy and content
patterns.lead: how the corpus writes — numbers where a generated page puts adjectives, verbs where it puts nouns, a register that switches only at chapter boundaries, a conversion sized to the decision, chrome that speaks the audience's own paperwork, and credibility carried as data. Read it while the brief is captured and again before the jury; cite it as `[pattern:copy-and-content#section]`. Site copy appears only in fragments, and every fragment is labelled; none is a line to reuse. `reflex-lists.md` holds the words to avoid and is not repeated here.

patterns.title: Cursor and pointer
patterns.lead: the pointer as an affordance system — the cursor that carries mass and meaning, the previews and reveals that chase it, the targets that pull on it, and the drags and holds that ask for a small physical commitment. It records what the corpus does with a fine pointer and what the plugin adds for coarse pointers and keyboards, because no card documents either. Cite as `[pattern:cursor-and-pointer#section]`.

patterns.title: GSAP choreography
patterns.lead: the deep GSAP path of `awards:motion` (`--gsap`). How the analysed sites structure GSAP across a whole page — timeline architecture, ScrollTrigger configurations as shipped, easing as actually used, SplitText, Flip and Observer choreography, and GL uniforms driven from timelines. It does not teach the API: that is GreenSock's official skills and `stacks/gsap-3.15.md`. Tokens, duration bands and scrub rules stay in `[pattern:motion-vocabulary]`. Cite as `[pattern:gsap-choreography#section]`. Every row carries the card's confidence label; structure read from minified bundles is `[inferred]`.

patterns.title: Hero archetypes
patterns.lead: the first viewports the corpus actually built — what each is made of, how it enters, what it does on a phone, what the DOM says underneath and which recipes build it. Read it after the narrative model is chosen and before the FIRST VIEWPORT line of the direction contract is written; cite it as `[pattern:hero-archetypes#archetype]`. An archetype is a structure with a card attached; the card's signature — its device, its object, its colour — is exactly what is not taken.

patterns.title: House tells — this plugin's own defaults, dated
patterns.lead: the fourth rut. The category rut, the Awwwards rut and the template skeleton are other people's defaults; this file lists the shapes this plugin's own finished builds converge on, so concept can name them and refuse them, and the jury can count them. Each wave is dated and never rewritten: a device that was a fresh idea in one wave is a habit by the next, which is exactly how every generated look starts. Read it in concept Step 1, before the seven worlds, and in the jury's slop scan.

patterns.title: Internationalisation and commerce
patterns.lead: two things an award site meets after the comp is approved. Part A is a second language that breaks the display type, the splits and the motion direction: locales, scripts, right-to-left, fonts, hreflang and a pseudo-locale check. Part B is a shop whose purchase path has to survive the motion layer: the product card, price and variants, quick add, the cart drawer and the hand-off to a hosted checkout. Read Part A when the brief names more than one language, and Part B when anything is sold. Cite it as `[pattern:i18n-and-commerce#section]`. The corpus is thin on both: no card records a right-to-left locale, and no card captured a cart, a product route or a checkout. Where this file has no card, it says so and states a plugin rule.

patterns.lead: the imagery decision every direction contract has to make, and the sourcing, generation and licence record behind every asset a build ships. The rubric's Content anchors at 9 and 10 ask for real photography or renders authored at full fidelity (`references/jury/rubric.md`); a build that defaults to type on a flat ground has made no imagery decision at all.

patterns.title: Inner pages
patterns.lead: the routes behind the home page. It covers the case study, the project or product detail, the article, about, contact and enquiry, the index or archive, and the 404. For each it gives the job, a structure that suits it, and how the home page's world carries in without repeating the hero, plus the transitions between home and inner routes. Read it when `structure` writes the page map for more than one route. Cite it as `[pattern:inner-pages#section]`.

patterns.title: Layout and composition
patterns.lead: the geometry under each chapter — columns, gutters and margins, line length and where the text column sits, how much of the viewport is picture, when a section touches the glass, and how space between chapters is paced. Read it while writing `DESIGN.md ## Layout` and filling the Layout column of `AWARDS.md ## Page map`; cite it as `[pattern:layout-and-composition#section]`. Scaling systems and phone checks are in `[pattern:responsive-strategy#decide-before-build]`, first-viewport anatomy in `[pattern:hero-archetypes#choosing]`, type sizes in `[pattern:typography#fluid-scale]`. Where one cell cites several cards, its uses are listed in the order the cards are cited.

patterns.title: Motion vocabulary
patterns.lead: the shared grammar of movement across the corpus — which curves, durations and staggers the award-winning sites actually use, how they feed scroll and pointer velocity into motion, which scroll model each one chose and why, and the three motion tiers every page ships. Read it before writing any tween; cite it as `[pattern:motion-vocabulary#section]`. Parameters come from the site cards and carry their confidence labels; where the corpus is silent, the plugin's own defaults are named as such.

patterns.title: Narrative structures
patterns.lead: the eight ways the corpus turns a page into a story — the chapter beats each model runs, where it places its one interruption, how it closes, which register its copy speaks and what the DOM must still say with CSS off. Read it during concept and structure work, before the page map is written; cite it as `[pattern:narrative-structures#model]`. Every model is a principle with cards attached, never a section order to reproduce: each card's §8 names the literal order it refuses.

patterns.title: Negative exemplars
patterns.lead: three pages that show what the corpus principles are measured against, captured at desktop and phone and stored beside this file in `negative/`. Every one is synthetic and built by this plugin: two are eval fixtures, one is assembled from the plugin's own former defaults. Open the frames when a direction, a first viewport or a jury score needs a picture of the failure, not a description of it. Each is paired with the principle it fails and the audit rules that catch what can be caught.

patterns.title: Performance: INP and CLS
patterns.lead: the two field metrics a motion-heavy page loses without noticing. INP covers how fast the page answers a click, tap or key. CLS covers how far the layout jumps while it loads. Both are decided by the motion layer, not by asset weight. LCP and the weight budgets live in `[pattern:asset-pipeline#budgets]` and `[pattern:asset-pipeline#staged-loading]`, and font loading lives in `[pattern:typography#loading]`. This file does not repeat them. Read it before the motion score is built and again before `ship`. Cite it as `[pattern:performance-cwv#section]`. The thresholds below are the platform's own. Corpus figures come from headless SwiftShader captures and are signals, never field data.

patterns.title: Preloaders and transitions
patterns.lead: the first moment and the in-between moments — how the corpus turns loading into the opening beat of the story, and how it moves between routes, sections and themes without a hard cut. It lists the archetypes actually seen, the mechanics behind them, and the rules that keep a loader from becoming a wall. Cite as `[pattern:preloaders-and-transitions#section]`.

patterns.title: Responsive strategy
patterns.lead: the decision that has to be made before the first component exists — how the layout scales, what a coarse pointer swaps out, whether the phone gets its own experience or a degraded one, and what the GL layer may cost on a mobile GPU. The corpus offers two scaling systems and two mobile philosophies; it offers almost no touch-target, zoom or reflow evidence, so those rules are the plugin's own and are marked as such. Cite as `[pattern:responsive-strategy#section]`.

patterns.title: SEO and semantics

recipes.title: Optional auto-scroll that any user input hands back
recipes.summary: An `aria-pressed` Auto toggle, off on every visit, advances Lenis by `90 px × dt` on the shared ticker (`lenis.scrollTo(y, { immediate: true })` from a float accumulator, `dt` clamped to `100 ms`); a capture-phase wheel, touchstart, pointerdown or keydown anywhere but the toggle hands control back at once, as does any scroll more than `3 px` from where it was written (scrollbar, find-in-page, a link) and reaching the end; each change written once to a polite `role="status"` line; under reduced motion and static the toggle stays focusable but `aria-disabled`, with the reason in its description

recipes.title: Auto-advancing tabs with a visible clock

recipes.title: Centred carousel with blur-peek neighbours and a velocity-graded snap
recipes.summary: Centred card sharp, neighbours at `.2` + `blur(6px)` (`.1`, no blur, ≤ 920 px), gap computed from a fixed peek (`10 %` / `14 %` of the width), release speed picks the snap (`> 1.2 px/ms` → `320 ms` crisp curve, slow `450–600 ms` soft curve), rubber-band overscroll returned by a critically damped spring stepped exactly with the shared ticker's `dt`; links in a list with roving `tabindex`, arrow / Home / End keys, a live "n of N"; blur kept but instant, snaps instant under reduced motion

items.title: Recipe drafts and a Drafts tab
items.body: Proposed recipes now wait in `recipes/_drafts/<id>/`, outside the catalogue and its counts, until the maintainer decides on them. The recipe explorer has a Drafts tab that runs each draft live beside its files, with a decision form: Accept, Improve with notes, or Reject. Under `npm run dev` the decision is saved to the draft's `review.json`. `scripts/drafts.mjs` starts a draft (from a template or from an existing recipe), answers an Improve (`reply`, which sends it back as Revised), promotes an accepted draft (paths, `added` date, frame, catalogue, explorer and quoted counts in one step) and drops a rejected one. `verify-recipes --drafts` and `gallery-frames --drafts` cover them, and CI audits and builds them with the recipes.

items.title: Thirteen recipe drafts, waiting for review
items.body: `chapter-jump-rail`, `local-search-dialog`, `prism-flip-label`, `map-pins-cards`, `news-read-state`, `homography-matrix3d-warp`, `flip-scroll-path`, `dealt-sheets-stage`, `scroll-curl-screens`, `character-splay-3d`, `pointer-repel-field`, `gl-erosion-dissolve` and `gl-product-configurator`, from catalogue entries that had no recipe and from unbuilt proposals. Each was reviewed independently across behaviour, verifier, accessibility, evidence and craft, and fixed after its findings were confirmed. They are not in the catalogue until promoted.

items.title: Token rules read one palette at a time
items.body: `audit.mjs` measured one page's ink on another page's paper when a folder held several pages with their own palettes, and the result depended on directory order. C01 (tokens), C02 and C03 now read each stylesheet that declares its own ground and ink alone; a project with one palette is read as before.

items.title: Son Daven's video weave, read again (corpus wave 6a)
items.body: At the maintainer's request, a deep re-read of `son-daven` focused on the effect that weaves every picture on the site, film included, into its two brand tokens and closes the page in the footer. The card's §3–§6 are rewritten from the whole renderer with a `### Tech lens: WebGL`: clips graded on black composited as keyed layers, one bar per cell from the tone, levels and boxes as GSAP tween targets, fifteen contexts on the home page, a load gate with no ceiling, three HEVC-only clips. The findings went into the WebGL and transition playbooks and the webgl, structure and component skills.

items.title: Three recipes from Son Daven
items.body: `gl-video-dither-layers` (keyed footage woven into the close as bars, or as an ASCII glyph ramp sorted by measured ink; footage as `<video>`, uploaded once per frame; a pause control), `gl-dither-scene-pool` (the weave on every picture of a page from one WebGL context: slices copied into in-flow canvases, pooled clips, seasons swapped by levels) and `dither-cell-transition` (one woven curtain for the arrival and every route, a load gate with a ceiling, focus and scroll rules). Each passes `verify-recipes --only` and `--pseudo`; SwiftShader only.

items.title: Corpus wave 6b, The Line with a motion lens
items.body: Run beside 6a as a separate task: a live re-read of `the-line` over the home route, `/work` and one case study. The site's bundle is unchanged since September; the pass read the component chunks the first one did not: four registered blink effects, CustomEases built from the CSS curves, dealt sheets on per-item rails, a footer held on a rail with credits under a lifting stage, a row marker that cuts, a twelve-item grid cycle, and a case-to-case transition that moves the live nodes into the next hero. A keyboard walk found 17 of 58 tab stops focused under the closing sheet. Folded into nine pattern files and the motion, structure and component skills.

items.title: Three recipes from The Line, 102 entries in all
items.body: `footer-credits-hinge` (a closing sheet over a held footer, credits under it, `inert` while closed, focus never under the sheet), `overprint-marker-index` (one multiply marker cut between rows, on pointer, keyboard and a touch reading line, with announced sorting) and `next-case-handoff` (a close that becomes the next page's hero, its live media node reparented, real links underneath). Not yet measured on a real GPU, phone or Safari.

items.title: One encoded clip, scrubbed frame by frame
items.body: `webcodecs-frame-scrub` builds the decoder Son Daven ships unused: the chunks of one clip and a manifest of their offsets in a single file, WebCodecs decoding exactly the frame the scroll names, a keyframe every ten frames, requests made during a seek coalesced to the newest instead of resetting the decoder, the frames passed on the way kept as bitmaps for scrubbing back, every `VideoFrame` closed. The demo encodes its drawn film on load; 120 frames are about 255 KB as one H.264 stream against 772 KB as WebP stills. Without WebCodecs the frames are drawn directly; reduced motion shows one still. An edge code on the film lets the verifier read the frame on screen. 103 entries in all.

items.title: A New label in the recipe explorer
items.body: `recipe.json` takes an optional `added` date (`build-catalogue.mjs` checks the form). A recipe added within 30 days of the newest one carries a small New label on its plate, in the index and in the stage, which also lists the date; searching "new" finds them. The window counts from the newest date in the catalogue, not today, so the generated page does not change on its own. The seven recipes of this branch carry it.

items.title: Captures of pages that never finish loading
items.body: `capture.mjs` captured nothing and called a page unreachable when its `load` event never fired inside the timeout; it now captures once the document has parsed and lists the viewport in `manifest.loadTimeouts`. The research skill reads a gate that never opens as a finding. A behavior check covers it.

items.title: Found pictures off
items.body: `craft` and `concept` take `--no-found-pictures`, or a brief that rules out outside pictures, and write `Found pictures: off` on the `## Budgets & tiers` line of `AWARDS.md`, for that build only. Concept then skips the open-collection search and goes from the client's own pictures straight to made imagery. `assets.mjs search` and `get` refuse with exit 3 while the line stands. The jury does not count code-only imagery as a `House concept` row, and `house-ledger.mjs --against` reports it without counting it. Made imagery still needs its three levels of detail. `--found-pictures`, or setting the line to `search`, turns the rule back on. A missing line reads as `search`, so existing builds are unchanged.

intro: From the comparison with taste-skill v2.1.5 (`docs/handoff/analysis-2026-10-26-taste-skill.md`), all twelve of its recommendations, plus corpus wave 5 and the recipe explorer.
Also in this release, from the work merged since 0.8.0:

items.title: The plugin's own rut
items.body: The five builds of 2026-10-23 shared one concept shape: the page as an object, the scroll as a process with a readout in the margin, code-only imagery on a light duotone. `references/patterns/house-tells.md` dates those shapes as a wave; concept names them as a fourth rut beside the category, Awwwards and template ruts, and the jury counts them as the `House concept` slop family. `scripts/house-ledger.mjs` reads finished builds' contracts and says which features are spent (`docs/handoff/house-ledger.md`, generated, held by check-sync), and `--against AWARDS.md` exits 2 when a new contract shares two or more.

items.title: The subject first
items.body: Concept writes an inventory of eight to twelve things that belong to this client and no competitor onto the Brief's `Inventory` line, builds worlds on them, and ends THESIS with a competitor test: the nearest real competitor's name in the thesis, and why it breaks. The jury names its own competitor and caps Creativity at 7 when the page would serve it as well. THESIS refusals are written for the subject, not copied from the template, and the first idea that came to mind is refused unless it passes.

items.title: Outside entropy in the deal
items.body: Fourteen concept engines (`scripts/data/engines.json`, each with the cards that run it) and a deck of forty-four stimuli from outside any category (`scripts/data/stimuli.json`). `roll.mjs --stimulus 2` deals two before the worlds are written and worlds 6 and 7 fuse them with inventory items; `--engines` deals three worlds from three engines and `--avoid` keeps spent engines back; `--choose` deals a colour strategy or a hero archetype among the ones the contract allows. Every existing seed deals as before.

items.title: Real pictures
items.body: `assets.mjs search` asks Openverse, the Met, the Art Institute of Chicago, NASA, the Library of Congress and Wikimedia Commons (footage: Commons, the Internet Archive, NASA) at once, keeps only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA, and `assets.mjs get` downloads a result and logs its credit. With no assets, found pictures of the subject's world now come before made imagery; made imagery needs three levels of detail. `capture.mjs` records how much of each frame is photograph and how much is made imagery (`metrics.<viewport>.pictures`), which the jury reads.

items.title: The frame, measured
items.body: Rendered rules L11 (text, a heading or an action covered at every scroll position where it is in view, with canvases and decorative layers hit-tested), L12 (unequal outer margins), L13 (a lopsided desktop section), L14 (running text with no heading), L15 (two or more near-empty screens) and S11 (no readable h1 1.2 s after load, a P3 note). Headline line counts and first-viewport actions are measured for the jury, not ruled. 95 rules.

items.title: The keyboard and thumb walk
items.body: `capture.mjs --walk` tabs through every stop and back, opens each disclosure with Enter and tries Shift+Tab and Escape on it, presses each button, and taps each control on a phone; `walk.json` is the evidence for the jury's usability walk steps 1 and 2, and jury, ship and component capture with it.

items.title: Blueprints and budgets
items.body: Every hero archetype has a desktop and phone blueprint in numbers, from the cards' measured fingerprints; the hero probe writes where the hero departs from it. `copy-and-content.md#headline-budget` gives the two-line arithmetic and the statement rule. The layout, motion and preloader files gain measured figures from beyond the corpus, marked as such, and no loader is the default.

items.title: Measurement
items.body: `evals/tournament.mjs` prepares a blind tournament (same briefs, several arms, frames under shuffled letters, a private key) and reveals it, counting only reasoned judgements and reporting how often judges grouped one arm's builds as the same tool; `jury --blind` judges one; `evals/visual/tournament.md` is the protocol. `scripts/contrast-set.mjs` runs the rendered audit on corpus winners and on unawarded pages and tabulates which rules separate them (`references/sites/_prevalence.md`, a first pilot). Its first run caught two of this release's own rules firing on most winners: L11 counted clouds, curtains and stacked panels passing over a title, and S11 counted loaders, entrances and film-first openings. L11 now counts only text that is never readable, and a pixel comparison (the text's box with the cover shown and hidden) confirms every candidate the hit test proposes, which took it from six of seven winners to two of seven and none of the six unawarded pages, as real overlaps rather than a style; S11 is a P3 note; the contrast set re-measures whenever the audit changes.

items.title: Smaller
items.body: Controls that explain themselves (component); the jury triggers when an award-level page looks generic, templated or AI-made; contract graders for the inventory, the competitor line and the engines on the Seed line; deal graders for the stimuli and the engine tags.

items.title: Upgrading from 0.8
items.body: A major version because a build is now asked different things: the concept round writes an `Inventory` line in `## Brief`, ends THESIS with `Competitor test:`, and records `ENGINES`, `STIMULI` and the locked `ENGINE` on the Seed line. Nothing rewrites an existing `AWARDS.md`: in a 0.8 build the new lines stay empty until concept runs again, and `house-ledger.mjs` infers what an older contract does not declare. The rendered audit adds L11 at P2, so a page that passed 0.8 can newly report text it never lets a visitor read.

items.title: Corpus wave 5 with a WebGL and 3D lens
items.body: Four sites the maintainer named, read over the hero, nav, footer and whole page: a lens pass on `oryzo`, and new cards for `daikifujita`, `da-san333` and `everswap`. The index grows from 62 to 65 rows; the WebGL playbooks gain their teardown rows, post chains and effect parameters.

items.title: Seven new recipes, 96 entries
items.body: A footer swarm lit by an occupancy atlas, screen paint that bends the whole page, grade-pass scene cuts (blur dip, frozen-frame iris, footer close), a glass object that refracts the page's own words on section anchors, a pointer wake that opens a world under the hero, a point cloud that morphs between SVG shapes on a 2D canvas, and a header logo that is the hero's wordmark.

items.title: Not yet measured
items.body: The seven recipes ran on SwiftShader only; no real GPU or phone pass.

items.title: A recipe explorer
items.body: `recipes/index.html`, the page `npm run dev` opens, is now an explorer instead of a list: a contact sheet of all 96 frames (wave 5's seven included), plates grouped by the catalogue with search, faceted filters (group, library, input, technique, WebGL, component, concern) and tiers, an index layout with a following preview, plates that run live under a resting pointer, and a stage that runs one recipe at desktop or phone size beside its manifest, README and source, with a scroll scrubber marked at the verifier's positions and a play-through. Generated from the manifests by `scripts/build-gallery.mjs` (check-sync holds it), frames from `scripts/gallery-frames.mjs`; readable without script, light and dark, P0–P3 clean under `audit.mjs --render`.

intro: From the 2026-10-22 review, batches 1 to 5 (everything except the large, lower-impact items), and the plugin's own site rebuilt and shipped by the plugin's own loop.

items.title: Truthful rendered checks
items.body: Every visible text is measured against what is actually behind it, focus states included (C01, A12); axe-core runs WCAG 2.2 A/AA (A16); new rules for titles, descriptions, canonical and Open Graph (S07–S10), skip links (A13), touch targets (A14) and duplicate ids (A15). A rendered step that fails is an `ERR` finding, never a clean read; a bundler project renders its build output. Rendered checks run at desktop, tablet and phone and add blank viewports (L09), lopsided tablet and phone sections (L10) and layout shift during load (P08). 85 rules.

items.title: Evidence the jury can use
items.body: Tablet frames, ARIA trees, held-clock timeline frames and a contact sheet, a video pass, a throttled phone pass, a GPU lane that refuses SwiftShader, per-frame diffs against the previous round, and Chrome UX Report field data (`scripts/crux.mjs`). The jury scores Awwwards' six developer criteria by name.

items.title: Recipes fixed by the sweeps
items.body: Five recipes overflowed a phone, left a blank tablet screen or shifted during load; all five are fixed, and the shared `--muted` ink clears AA everywhere.

items.title: Upkeep
items.body: `scripts/check-versions.mjs` compares every pin with the registry; the doctor checks the running Node against every installed package's `engines.node` and asks for 22 LTS or 24 LTS; `scripts/calibration.mjs` recomputes the rubric's corpus figures from the cards; Playwright 1.64.1 is pinned in the recipes, and recipe stamping is opt-in.

items.title: Evals
items.body: Contract, resume and coexist tiers (the last beside GreenSock's gsap-skills), near-miss negatives, a bland-but-clean jury case, a free regrade of kept runs and a picker that maps a diff to the cases it needs.

items.title: Platform
items.body: Shorter skill descriptions (7.4k characters in all, inside Codex's budget), a SubagentStop check that sends a jury reply without its disposition line back once, `userConfig` for the hooks and the default stack, a narrower jury toolset with Write, 45 turns and no CLAUDE.md, `scripts/awards-log.mjs` for log and Status lines, research that honours the site owner's policy (`scripts/policy.mjs`), scoped exceptions (`C01@path`), a portable capture lock, a hardened local server, sub-skill hand-offs that keep craft's pre-jury checks, and a deal that fits the question tool.

items.title: Imagery and assets
items.body: WORLD names an imagery strategy and what supplies it; `references/patterns/imagery-and-assets.md` covers the strategies the cards use, open sources, generated assets (with the EU AI Act's transparency rules from 2 August 2026) and the asset log `scripts/assets.mjs` keeps in `.awards/assets.json`.

items.title: Less house style, more mechanism
items.body: No default motion register; labels untracked unless WORLD asks; the fullscreen menu loses its numbers by default; every recipe use carries a `keep / change / pair` line; faces are chosen character first from Fontsource with `scripts/fonts.mjs` (a seeded pull, a rendered specimen of the real headline, the licence on fetch).

items.title: What finish looks like, and what failure looks like
items.body: craft-floor names the finish beside the prohibitions; `references/patterns/negative-exemplars.md` pairs three captured failures (the house style, the template product page, the clean but forgettable page) with the rules they break; rendered rules X21 (eyebrow labels by computed style) and P09 (images drawn above their natural size).

items.title: Composition you can measure
items.body: `references/patterns/layout-and-composition.md` (grids, gutters, measure, image share, thirteen layout families and the adjacency rules the page map is checked against), and a block-map skeleton plus a measured fingerprint row (type ramp at 1440 and 390, margin, column edges, media share) for every card that allows it (`scripts/skeleton.mjs`, `references/sites/_fingerprints.md`).

items.title: A corpus that keeps itself honest
items.body: The index is generated from the card headers (`build-index.mjs`), every card is checked against a vocabulary (`check-card.mjs`), waves are opened against a gap report (`corpus-gaps.mjs`) after a model-free pre-pass (`corpus-prepass.mjs`), a quarterly health pass records which sites were rebuilt (`corpus-health.mjs`), research reads up to two named inner routes, and the clone-level card is cited as `[clone:floema-jewelry]`.

items.title: Recipe catalogue from data
items.body: `recipes/README.md` is generated from each `recipe.json` (intent, group, summary), grouped by the component catalogue, with tags from a controlled vocabulary.

items.title: New modes
items.body: `craft --quick` for one landing page (system and structure checked once, no component passes, one jury round); `craft redesign <url|dir>` (a branch, a baseline capture and a forked `jury --baseline`, a content inventory, two baseline faults as THESIS refusals); `capture.mjs --routes` captures every route of a site into one `routes.json` the jury reads; award program presets (`jury --program awwwards,cssda,fwa,webby`, `references/jury/programs.md`); DESIGN.md lint, export and per-round token diffs through Google's design.md CLI (`scripts/design-md.mjs`).
